name: Selank

card.summary: A Russian-developed anxiolytic peptide that forum users group with Semax as a nootropic; human evidence is limited to a few Russian-language studies.
card.note: Approved only in Russia; products sold elsewhere are unregulated research chemicals.

quick.overview:
Selank is a synthetic seven-amino-acid peptide derived from tuftsin, developed in Russia and registered there as nasal drops for anxiety. On looksmax.org it is discussed alongside Semax and Cerebrolysin as a nootropic, with members asking whether such peptides are "cope".

It has no connection to physical appearance; its place in the community is as a cognition and mood supplement. Published research is mostly animal and in-vitro work, much of it from Russian groups.
quick.mechanism: Studies in cells and animals suggest it may influence GABA-related gene expression and inhibit enkephalin-degrading enzymes, which researchers propose as routes to its anxiolytic effects.
quick.risks: It is a registered drug only in Russia. Outside Russia it is sold as a research chemical without regulatory oversight. A 2021 pharmacology review grouped it among agents acting on GABA receptors.

lead: Selank is a synthetic heptapeptide (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) designed as a longer-lasting analog of tuftsin, a tetrapeptide fragment of immunoglobulin G. It was developed at the Institute of Molecular Genetics of the Russian Academy of Sciences together with the Zakusov Institute of Pharmacology [1].

Reference works describe it as having been registered in Russia in 2009 as intranasal drops for generalized anxiety disorder [1]. Published studies include animal behavioural experiments and biochemical work on enkephalin-degrading enzymes and GABAergic gene expression [2][3][4].
Within looksmaxxing communities, Selank is discussed as a nootropic, usually together with Semax. No published trial has examined it for appearance outcomes.
infobox: Prescription drug in Russia; unapproved elsewhere

paras: In vitro work reported that Selank and Semax inhibit enkephalin-degrading enzymes in human serum, which authors proposed as a possible basis of its anxiolytic activity [5][6]. A 2017 cell-culture study found it altered expression of genes involved in GABAergic neurotransmission [7], and a 2018 review summarised molecular aspects of its activity [8].
Glyproline peptides (those containing proline-glycine-proline motifs) have been described as unusually stable for regulatory peptides, and Selank has been studied alongside them [9].

No studies found in the available sources for appearance outcomes. For its approved anxiety use, the sources describe Russian clinical work, but the studies reviewed here are animal or laboratory studies: rodent experiments of tuftsin-family peptides under conflict-stress conditions reported anti-stress behavioural effects [10], and a rat study reported Selank enhanced the anxiety-reducing effect of diazepam under chronic mild stress [11].

Looksmax.org threads ask how Selank differs from Semax and whether Semax, Selank and Cerebrolysin are "cope" [12][13]. Replies in such threads are often joking or terse, and members describe themselves as unfamiliar with the compounds. Sellers market it as a research peptide outside Russia.

timeline.event: Developed in Russia as a tuftsin analog [1]
Registered in Russia for generalized anxiety disorder [1]

lore.intro: Selank appears on looksmax.org mainly in questions about Semax and nootropics rather than as an appearance compound [12][13].

claims.claim: Selank and Semax are useful nootropics for focus and mood.
claims.believers: Some members ask for experiences with the pair and for guidance on when to use each [12][13].
claims.experts: Published research is largely animal and cell studies, many from Russian groups [10][11][7].

claims.believers: Other members dismiss them as cope, while the original poster in one thread says replies were mostly trolling [13][14].
claims.experts: No published studies have tested them against looksmaxxing goals.
